Leah C: Heads up—noticed flaky auth retries in the Android sample when using our corporate proxy + OkHttp 4.x. Authenticator returns a rebuilt request with Authorization header, but the server sees no Authorization. Only repros with proxy enabled.

Ravi M: Are you using an application interceptor to add the header or a network interceptor? Authenticator retries can interact weirdly with proxy hops.

Leah C: App interceptor normally adds header. Authenticator does a sync token refresh with Retrofit.execute() and returns original.newBuilder().header("Authorization", token).build(). Logs show header present in OkHttp request object but wire capture from the upstream shows it missing.

Ravi M: Proxy suspicion makes sense. Proxies and 407 flows can cause hop-by-hop header stripping. Quick workaround: add a tiny network interceptor that ensures Authorization exists right before chain.proceed(). That fixed it for me in a quick test.

Leah C: Network interceptor works as a band-aid but breaks some unit tests that assert earlier interception. Thinking to keep app interceptor + network safety patch that copies token from TokenStore if header missing.

Ravi M: Sounds reasonable. Also add a note in the sample app docs: when running behind corporate proxies use network-level safeguard and avoid doing synchronous refreshes on the same client to prevent deadlocks. If you can create a minimal OkHttp-only repro (no Retrofit), we should file an upstream issue.

sdk-bot: [ci] devex/sample-app (android)  smoke-tests  FAILED  flaky on proxy scenario

Leah C: I'll open a small PR with the network-safeguard + docs note and try to produce a stripped-down repro for OkHttp. Thanks for the suggestions.
